stories.title: CISA Says Attackers Are Exploiting Two Critical Citrix NetScaler Flaws Globally
Attackers Bypass WAFs to Exploit Oracle PeopleSoft Flaw and Deploy Web Shells
stories.abstract: The ShinyHunters extortion group is actively exploiting CVE-2026-35273 in Oracle PeopleSoft. Attackers are utilizing URL-encoding techniques to circumvent existing web application firewall protections, enabling them to successfully target and compromise vulnerable servers despite previous mitigation efforts.
stories.why: This bypass renders existing WAF rules ineffective, allowing threat actors to regain access to previously secured environments.
stories.action: Apply the latest Oracle security patches for CVE-2026-35273 immediately.

stories.title: WSO2 and Adobe Commerce Flaws Exploited in Attacks, Added to CISA KEV
SharePoint RCE and MikroTik RouterOS Flaws Actively Exploited in the Wild
stories.abstract: CISA has added a critical code injection vulnerability in Microsoft SharePoint, tracked as CVE-2026-65660, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw is currently being leveraged in active cyberattacks, prompting urgent remediation requirements for federal agencies.
stories.why: This vulnerability allows for remote code execution, posing a severe risk of system compromise and unauthorized access to sensitive enterprise data.
stories.action: Apply the latest security updates for Microsoft SharePoint immediately.

stories.title: Warning: Two Unpatched Citrix NetScaler RCE Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation
stories.abstract: Citrix has released patches for eight vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and Gateway, including two critical remote code execution flaws currently being exploited by attackers. One of these vulnerabilities impacts all affected versions, even those using default configurations.
stories.why: Unauthenticated RCE vulnerabilities in edge infrastructure are prime targets for initial access and persistent network compromise.
stories.action: Update all Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway instances immediately and perform a compromise assessment.

stories.title: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
JADEPUFFER-Linked Attackers Used Compromised Service Principals to Delete Azure Resources
stories.abstract: The threat actor Storm-3168, known as JadePuffer, utilized compromised service principals to infiltrate Azure environments. Over an 18-hour period, the group performed reconnaissance and credential harvesting before systematically deleting cloud storage, databases, and application resources to cause significant operational disruption.
stories.why: This highlights the danger of compromised service principals and the shift toward automated, agentic attacks capable of rapid, large-scale cloud infrastructure destruction.
stories.action: Audit and rotate all service principal credentials and enforce strict least-privilege access controls.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit WordPress CVE-2026-87902 Within Hours of Disclosure
Citrix Patches Critical Zero Days Under Active Exploitation
stories.abstract: Citrix has acknowledged that two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in its software are currently being leveraged by malicious actors in active exploitation campaigns.
stories.why: Unauthenticated remote code execution flaws in edge infrastructure represent a high-risk vector for initial network compromise and lateral movement.
stories.action: Apply the latest Citrix security patches immediately.

stories.title: Bitget resumes Bitcoin withdrawals after $387.5 million crypto heist
Former US soldier gets nearly six-year sentence for hacking, extorting telecoms
stories.abstract: A former U.S. Army soldier received a 70-month prison sentence for infiltrating multiple telecommunications firms. The perpetrator stole sensitive metadata belonging to over 100 million customers and engaged in extortion schemes against at least ten technology companies between 2023 and 2024.
stories.why: This case highlights significant vulnerabilities in telecom data security and the severe insider threat risks posed by individuals with technical expertise.

stories.title: Certainties in life: Death, taxes, and critical Citrix vulns under attack
stories.abstract: Citrix has released emergency patches for its NetScaler appliances, addressing three critical vulnerabilities alongside five additional high-severity security flaws. Administrators should prioritize these updates to mitigate potential exploitation risks within their infrastructure.
stories.why: NetScaler devices are frequent targets for initial access brokers and state-sponsored actors due to their position at the network perimeter.
stories.action: Apply the latest NetScaler security patches immediately.

stories.title: Linux security advisory (AV26-970)
wolfSSL security advisory (AV26-969)
IBM security advisory (AV26-967)
Dell security advisory (AV26-966)
stories.abstract: Dell has released security patches addressing multiple vulnerabilities across several products, including Rugged Control Center, Secure Connect Gateway Policy Manager, ThinOS 10, and Trusted Device Client. Administrators should review the specific advisories for each affected component to mitigate potential security risks.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in management and endpoint software can provide attackers with unauthorized access or privilege escalation paths within enterprise environments.
stories.action: Update Rugged Control Center, Secure Connect Gateway, ThinOS, and Trusted Device Client to the latest versions.

stories.title: Modulate Raises $25 Million to Advance Deepfake Detection
stories.abstract: Modulate secured $25 million in funding to expand its AI-driven platform. The company focuses on real-time detection of synthetic voice technology to combat fraud, scams, and malicious deepfake content within digital communication environments.
stories.why: As AI-generated voice cloning becomes more sophisticated, automated detection tools are increasingly necessary to verify identity and prevent social engineering attacks.

New Mexico jury finds Meta deceived consumers about data privacy practices
Kiteworks Urges Server Shutdown, Finds Advanced Forms Vulnerability
Bitget Says Attacker Exploited Third-Party Security Product Flaw to Steal $388M
Prison Sentence for Former US Soldier Who Hacked AT&T and Verizon
stories.abstract: A former U.S. soldier received a 70-month prison sentence for orchestrating a scheme to illicitly access and steal sensitive data from AT&T and Verizon wireless networks.
stories.why: Highlights the ongoing threat of insider-style attacks and the severe legal consequences for individuals who compromise telecommunications infrastructure.

stories.title: Carbonato Botnet Compromises Docker Hosts to Deploy Telegram-Controlled Hermes AI Agent
stories.abstract: The Carbonato botnet is actively exploiting misconfigured Docker daemons to install the Hermes AI agent. Once deployed, the malware modifies the agent's persona file to accept and execute arbitrary commands issued via Telegram, effectively turning the AI framework into a remote access tool.
stories.why: Exposed Docker APIs are being weaponized to gain persistent remote control over containerized environments through AI-driven command execution.
stories.action: Secure Docker daemon ports and restrict access to authorized IP addresses only.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Monday, September 28th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10112, (Mon, Sep 28th)
Wireshark 4.6.9 Released, (Sun, Sep 27th)
stories.abstract: The Wireshark development team has released version 4.6.9, which addresses 19 distinct security vulnerabilities alongside 16 functional bugs identified within the network protocol analyzer.
stories.why: Unpatched network analysis tools can be exploited to achieve remote code execution or denial of service when processing malicious packet captures.

stories.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: $387M Crypto Hack, Citrix Exploits, AI Agents Go Off-Script, and More Threats
stories.abstract: Attackers hijacked a dormant domain previously used as placeholder text in approximately 1,700 software repositories. By registering the expired domain, threat actors began distributing malicious content to developers and systems relying on the legacy code references.
stories.why: Dependency confusion and stale code references create significant supply chain risks, allowing attackers to inject malicious payloads into trusted development environments.
stories.action: Audit repositories for dead links and expired domain references in documentation or configuration files.

stories.title: Misconfigured Supabase apps expose data in over 16,000 databases
stories.abstract: Security researchers identified over 16,000 misconfigured Supabase instances that inadvertently exposed sensitive data. These databases contained unprotected tables holding personally identifiable information, plaintext credentials, and authentication tokens, leaving them accessible to unauthorized parties over the public internet.
stories.why: Exposed databases provide attackers with immediate access to credentials and sensitive user data, facilitating account takeovers and further network compromise.
stories.action: Audit Supabase project permissions and ensure Row Level Security policies are correctly implemented.

stories.title: Compromised GitHub Actions Came Back Online and Resumed Executing Mini Shai-Hulud Malware
stories.abstract: Two GitHub Actions, previously compromised during the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign, were briefly re-enabled by their maintainer while still containing malicious code. The repositories have since been disabled again following public disclosure of the oversight.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks via compromised CI/CD pipelines can lead to unauthorized code execution and credential theft within automated build environments.
stories.action: Audit your workflow logs for any usage of actions-cool/issues-helper or actions-cool/maintain-one-comment.

stories.title: FBI Hackers Say They Won’t Publish Massive Trove of FBI Employee Data
stories.abstract: The hacking collective ShinyHunters claims they possess a significant database containing personal information on FBI personnel, including home addresses and family details. The group asserts they have no intention of releasing this sensitive information publicly.
stories.why: The potential exposure of federal law enforcement identities and locations poses severe physical security and counterintelligence risks.

stories.title: FBI reportedly declares ‘cyber security incident’ after hackers steal agents’ personal data
stories.abstract: The FBI is investigating a security breach involving the theft of sensitive personal data belonging to its personnel. Internal communications indicate that agents' Social Security numbers and other private information were compromised, though the agency has yet to issue a formal public statement.
stories.why: The exposure of federal law enforcement personnel data creates significant risks for targeted phishing, social engineering, and potential foreign intelligence exploitation.

stories.title: RatHat Android Malware Console Uses Gemini to Identify Higher-Value Victims
stories.abstract: The RatHat Android banking trojan operates via a malware-as-a-service model, providing individual operators with dedicated web consoles. These consoles manage infected devices and aggregate stolen data, with researchers identifying nearly 100 distinct deployments of the infrastructure since April 2026.
stories.why: The modular, distributed nature of this infrastructure complicates attribution and takedown efforts, while increasing the scale of mobile banking fraud campaigns.

Chrome Store Hosts 'Poper Blocker' Spyware Downloaded by Millions
IAM for AI agents: A Practical Enterprise Framework

80,000+ Organizations Had AI Logins Stolen: From Shadow AI to LLMjacking
stories.abstract: Infostealer malware has harvested credentials and session tokens for AI services across 80,000 corporate domains. These stolen accounts allow unauthorized access to sensitive internal conversations and enable LLMjacking, where attackers exploit enterprise AI resources for their own computational tasks.
stories.why: Compromised AI accounts provide attackers with a direct window into proprietary data and a vector to abuse expensive LLM infrastructure.
stories.action: Audit AI service logs for anomalous access and implement mandatory MFA for all enterprise AI platforms.
